sets.s: “Leanne is about to share her exam revision tips with her class.”
i: Leanne has revised for an exam before.
N
Leanne is sharing her exam revising tips with the rest of her class, but, whether or not she has sat an exam before, the statement does not make this assumption within itself.
Leanne has revision tips to share.
M
This assumption is made within the statement as she is about to share some information. The statement assumes that she has this information ready to be shared with the other people in her class.
The class needs Leanne to share her revision tips.
N
The statement just tells us what she is about to do, not why she is doing it, so the statement does not assume that the class needs or wants the information she is about to share.

sets.s: “Your second year of university will require a lot more work than the first, so you’ll have to organise your time more efficiently.”
i: The third year of university will be more difficult than the previous year.
N

There is no mention of the third year of university. The statement tells us that there will be more work for the second year, but the statement makes no assumption that the work which will have to be done will be any more difficult than it already is, so this assumption is not made in this statement.
The person receiving this information has the ability to organise their time more efficiently.
N
They are being told that they need to organise their time more efficiently, we do not know whether they have the ability to organise their time more efficiently. Therefore, assumption not made.
The person giving out this information has completed their second year at university.
N
This assumption is not being made in the statement, all that can be assumed is that they know the second year will be harder – not necessarily from experience.

sets.s: “Public transport is better for the environment than everyone using their own vehicles.”
i: Cars release more pollution than vehicles used in public transport.
N
This cannot be assumed as the statement is only comparing the use of public transport to everyone using their own vehicles, not just individual cars and buses.
Public transport is readily available to everyone.
N
The statement does not assume that public transport is available to everyone, just that if it were used by everyone over individual vehicles there would be an environmental benefit.
The use of public transport is encouraged.
M

The statement talks about public transport in a positive way and individual transport in a less positive way by comparing the two with each other, so the assumption that public transport is encouraged is made within the statement.

sets.s: “The peasants, workers, students and intelligentsia were right to engage in non-violent action in order to try and get the Czar to create an elected legislature in Russia.”
i: The Czar was pressured at the time to be able to create an elected legislature.
M

The statement implies that the group needed to engage in non-violent action towards the Czar to get the Czar to fulfil their request for an elected legislature. Therefore, this implies that the Czar was pressured and the assumption is made in the statement.
The Czar created an elected legislature.
N
The statement says they were right to do so, not that it was successful.
Some people in Russia wanted an elected legislature.
M
The statement talks about how the action-takers were right to do so, and that some Russian people did take action.
